Arenas , president for HGLS, said in a statement. “She will work closely with our worldwide teams to strengthen and build an ecosystem that encourages services to HYBE IP, a continued collaborative approach, and a focus on high impact. I’m grateful to have her on board to help execute the vision of a globally built platform powered by best-in-class services.”

Victor-Burkhardt added, “By helping artists grow from a first single to the global stage, my work has always been about strategically building careers that last. HYBE is redefining what a music company can be, and I’m excited to bring that experience to a global platform. Thank you to Isaac Lee [CEO, HYBE Americas] and Juan S. Arenas for this opportunity.”

P ophouse has appointed Kristina Heney and Greg Lombardo to the company’s leadership team. Heney has been named president, commercial and marketing, and is based in New York, while Lombardo is president, Pophouse Avatar Network, and is based in Los Angeles. Heney joins from Oak View Group, where she had served as executive vp, marketing, media and conferences. Lobardo had been vp and global head of experiences at Netflix.

“Pophouse was founded on the belief that the world’s most iconic artists can reach new generations through bold, imaginative experiences,” Jessica Koravos , CEO of Pophouse Entertainment, said in a statement. “Building on our partnerships with legendary artists and productions, including KISS, Iron Maiden, Tina Turner, Sia, Cyndi Lauper and Avicii, ABBA Voyage, Mamma Mia! The Party and our exhibitions, we aim to carry these legacies to audiences worldwide. Greg and Tina are two of the most accomplished leaders in live entertainment, and they bring exactly the combination of commercial discipline and creative ambition we need for the next chapter. I am delighted to welcome them both to our leadership team.”

entertainment.title: U2’s ‘Carnaval De Luz’ Becomes Its 12th U.K. No. 1 Album, Moving Band Up All-Time Leaderboard
entertainment.summary: It's the group's first No. 1 album of original material in 17 years.
entertainment.body:
U2 is No. 1 on the U.K.’s Official Albums Chart published Friday (Nov. 20) for a 12th time, this go-round with Carnaval De Luz . With this latest achievement, the band is third on the all-time rankings for groups.

The Irish group is now tied with Bruce Springsteen on the all-time list with 12 each, trailing only Elvis Presley (13), Madonna (13), Taylor Swift (14), The Rolling Stones (15), The Beatles (15) and Robbie Williams (16).

U2’s first No. 1 came in 1983 with third LP Boy , followed by The Unforgettable Fire (1984) , The Joshua Tree (1987), Rattle and Hum (1987), Zooropa (1993), Pop (1997), The Best of 1980-1990 (1998), All That You Can’t Leave Behind (2000), How to Dismantle an Atomic Bomb (2004), No Line on the Horizon (2009) and Songs of Surrender (2023).

entertainment.title: Jamie Miller’s ‘Babydoll’ Scores Fifth Consecutive Week as U.K.’s No. 1 Single
entertainment.summary: Justice scores its best-ever placing with GTA VI hit "Flower in a Hurricane."
entertainment.body:
Jamie Miller is No. 1 for a fifth week on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart with breakthrough single “Babydoll” on the list published Nov. 20.

The Cardiff-born singer first hit the top spot in October, becoming the first male Welsh solo act to hit the summit of the charts since Shakin’ Stevens in 1984. “Babydoll” is currently up to No. 37 on the Billboard Hot 100 , a new peak.

Speaking to Billboard in a recent Chartbreaker story, Miller commented on the song’s rapid rise. “It became this kind of phenomenon on TikTok,” he said of the track. “It feels like the song has kind of unified people, and it’s been so amazing to see how fun it’s been for everybody — from kids in Africa and people in Sweden to these amazing dance groups in America and TV shows in the U.K.”

Ashe’s “Stop the Wedding!” comes in at No. 2 and is a non-mover in the spot, her best-ever placing on the charts. Sombr’s “My Body Isn’t Ready” lifts two places to No. 3, and comes in the same week he was announced for a major slot at 2027’s Glastonbury Festival.

Tate McRae’s “Housewife” closes at No. 4, followed by Sienna Spiro’s previous chart-topper “Great Expectation” (No. 5).

As GTA VI launches globally , Justice’s “Flower in a Hurricane — a collaboration with SZA, Tame Impala and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard that appears on the soundtrack – hits a new peak at No 9, the duo’s best-ever placing on the charts to date.

A number of festive songs leap up the chart. Wham!’s “Last Christmas” is up to No. 12, Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” is at No. 18 and Olivia Rodrigo’s “Take Me Home (4 Christmas)” sits at No. 24.

entertainment.title: Tracker's Colter Shaw Teams Up With A Fellow Rewardist Played By Lost's Josh Holloway (Exclusive Sneak Peek)
entertainment.summary: TVLine has an exclusive sneak peek at Lost alum Josh Holloway as a rival rewardist who clashes with Justin Hartley's Colter Shaw in Tracker Season 4.
entertainment.body:
"Tracker" fans are already familiar with one of Colter Shaw's rival rewardists: Billie Matalon, his former associate and recurring love interest , played by Justin Hartley's real-life wife, Sofia Pernas. But now we're about to meet another — and he doesn't necessarily play by the same set of rules.

In TVLine's exclusive sneak peek from the Sunday, November 22 episode (CBS, 9:30/8:30c), Hartley's Colter crosses paths with Luke Kelso, a rival tracker played by "Lost" alum Josh Holloway . And while the two men may be in the same line of work, they clearly don't see eye to eye on how to get the job done.

Mike Taing/CBS The episode, titled "That's the Job," finds Colter hired to locate the owner of a small South Carolina inn, only for his search to put him at odds with Kelso, "whose reckless methods and questionable morals have put innocent lives at risk," according to the official description.

As the clip reveals, Kelso has been offered a whopping $100,000 to retrieve a man on behalf of a mysterious lawyer... and he doesn't seem particularly concerned about who hired him, or why.

"When it's that much, they don't pay you to ask questions," Kelso reasons.

"That's the difference between you and me," Colter counters. "I like to know what I'm getting into. I take a job, I want to know who hired me, and why."

Kelso's response? "That's real ethical and all, but I live in the real world. A job's a job."

"Tracker" Season 4 kicked off October 4 and set up a potential mystery involving a case Colter couldn't solve . More recently, in the November 15 episode, Reenie's assistant Mel finally met Colter in person and asked for his help filling in the missing pieces of her mother's murder — a storyline showrunner Elwood Reid previously told TVLine he was determined to resolve this season .

entertainment.title: Megan Moroney and Alex Warren Know a Good Song When They Hear It in the Car
entertainment.summary: For two artists whose lives revolve around music, the road offers a different kind of listening experience.
entertainment.body:
For country chart-topper Megan Moroney and pop hitmaker Alex Warren, a song isn’t necessarily finished when it leaves the studio. Sometimes, it needs a test drive.

For Warren, listening to music in the car holds sentimental meaning. On his new album, Wildchild , he pays tribute to his late father, who died of cancer when Warren was just nine years old. Some of his most powerful musical memories with his dad are inseparable from time spent in the car.

“My only memory of music growing up was getting in the car and listening to my dad’s CDs, and John Mayer was his guy,” Warren said. “When my dad passed away, I got in his car and [Mayer’s album] came on. When I wrote this song for my dad called ‘Wildchild,’ I put his voice on it, and I asked [Mayer] to do a guitar solo on it, so my dad and John have a song.”

The car is also where Warren discovered Moroney’s music. He recalls listening to her breakout hit “Tennessee Orange” in the car with his wife, who knew every word.

“She knows that song like the back of her hand, and it’s really cool because she applies it to her own life,” Warren said of Moroney’s autobiographical debut, which tells the story of a die-hard Georgia football fan falling for a Tennessee Volunteers fan.

“It encapsulates the kind of music my fans like,” said Moroney, whose sharp-eyed songwriting turns specific details into universal feelings that resonate with the masses.

“It’s creative, it’s honest, there’s the hook, and it’s storytelling. I feel like at the root of all of my songs, that’s what it is. And obviously I’m a Georgia Bulldog, so it’s just very me.”

Moroney and Warren may come from different corners of the music world, but the two found plenty of common ground during a conversation outside Fox & Locke, a storied live-music venue tucked into the rolling countryside of Leiper’s Fork, Tennessee. The discussion was part of Rolling Stone ’s Musicians on Musicians series. This time, Lexus sought to connect two artists from different backgrounds in an entirely new way by trading the usual lounge-like venues that host Musicians on Musicians conversations for the lounge-inspired quiet cabin of an all-electric 2027 Lexus TZ, which will make its debut this winter. entertainment.title: Farrah Fawcett Played 3 Characters On Her Husband's '70s Action Thriller Series
entertainment.summary: Farrah Fawcett played an astronaut, a reporter, and a chronic gambler in the hit Lee Majors sci-fi series "The Six Million Dollar Man."
entertainment.body:
ABC/Peacock Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Though she remains best known for "Charlie's Angels," Farrah Fawcett quit the show after just one season , and her resume is filled with other interesting projects. Her former husband, Lee Majors, was also a massive TV star in the 1970s, and Fawcett collaborated with him on more than one occasion. One of Majors' most popular projects was "The Six Million Dollar Man," one of the best shows of the 1970s .

Majors stars as Steve Austin, an astronaut who is fitted with expensive bionic parts after a near-death experience. Fawcett guest-starred in four episodes of the show, playing three different characters. In the Season 1 episode "Rescue of Athena One," she played Kelly Wood, who is set to become the first female American astronaut to go into space. Steve is tasked with training her. Fawcett returned as Kelly in the Season 4 episode "Nightmare in the Sky," in which she is accused of stealing an airplane during a test flight. Steve comes to her aid and clears her name.

In the Season 2 episode "The Peeping Blonde," Fawcett played the titular character, a reporter named Victoria Webster who discovers Steve's secret and wants to broadcast it to the world. She also starred in the Season 3 episode "The Golden Pharaoh" as Trish Hollander, a chronic gambler and former flame who assists Steve with recovering a stolen artifact. The first episode of "Charlie's Angels" aired just four days before Fawcett's final episode of "The Six Million Dollar Man," launching her to international stardom.

ABC/YouTube Both Farah Fawcett and Lee Majors appeared in numerous popular TV shows before their big breaks. Majors had a role in the hit Western series "The Virginian," while Fawcett appeared in "The Andy Griffith Show" spin-off "Mayberry R.F.D." In 1971, before "The Six Million Dollar Man" and "Charlie's Angels," Majors and Fawcett both featured in "Owen Marshall, Counselor at Law," a legal drama in which Arthur Hill plays the title character, a former prosecutor who switches over to the defense. Majors played Jess Brandon, a young lawyer assisting Marshall with his cases.

In Season 1, Fawcett appeared as Tori, the sister of a college student involved in a murder trial. Tori returned a few episodes later, with Brandon taking her on a date that's really a reconnaissance mission for a case. Two years later, in 1973, Fawcett and Majors tied the knot. They were married for nine years, though they separated in 1979. During this time they created a production company, Fawcett-Majors Productions. Some of their movies include the 1977 war drama "Just a Little Inconvenience," the 1978 historical adventure "The Norseman," and the 1979 horror flick "Killer Fish."

entertainment.title: Brandy Believes a ‘Moesha’ Reboot ‘Can Really Be Something in Today’s Time’
entertainment.summary: The "Have You Ever" singer floated a possible reboot on The Jennifer Hudson Show while reflecting on her reunion with Usher.
entertainment.body:
Brandy may have just delivered the theme song for Netflix’s A Different World reboot, but she might return to the studio to cut a new version of her Moesha theme song for a possible reboot!

During an interview on The Jennifer Hudson Show that aired Friday (Nov. 20), the Grammy-winning R&B icon reflected on her recent surprise appearance at Usher and Chris Brown’s R&B Tour, as well as a potential reboot of her classic ’90s coming-of-age sitcom, Moesha .

“I know I’ve said this in so many different places and so many different times,” Brandy began. “But Moesha can really be something in today’s time, especially since we’ve seen the success of [Netflix’s] A Different World [reboot]. I just really think that she could come back.”

Brandy starred in titular role of Moesha , which aired on UPN from 1996 to 2001. The beloved sitcom also starred Emmy-winning Abbott Elementary star Sheryl Lee Ralph and featured cameos from ’90s-defining Black megastars such as Usher and the late Kobe Bryant.

During Usher and Chris Brown’s R&B Tour stop at California’s SoFi Stadium on Sept. 26, Brandy made a surprise appearance during her former Moesha costar’s set for lively renditions of “Top of the World” and “I Wanna Be Down.” “It was so magical! I love Usher, I’m his biggest fan,” she gushed, later reminiscing on the playful vocal battles they waged backstage while on set. “And we worked together back in the day on Moesha . He was actually Moesha’s boyfriend, so we connected and the chemistry was unbelievable. Unmatched.”

Her pop-out previewed the Nov. 10 announcement of her and Monica’s The Boy Is Mine Las Vegas Residency. The run will consist of 10 shows between May 29 and July 17 at Resorts World Las Vegas, marking the first Sin City residency for both Grammy-winning R&B superstars.

The dynamic duo’s Vegas takeover follows their blockbuster arena-headlining Boy Is Mine Tour — both promoted by The Black Promoters Collective — which earned $44.7 million from 350,000 tickets sold across 32 shows, according to Billboard Boxscore. Both the tour and residency are named for the stars’ classic 1998 duet, which topped the Billboard Hot 100 for 13 weeks.

On Nov. 28, Brandy will star alongside her daughter Sy’Rai Smith in Lifetime’s new original holiday movie, Christmas Everyday: Married and Bright . The new film caps off a busy year for the mother-daughter duo; Brandy received her star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in March, while Sy’Rai dropped her debut studio album, Cold War , in August.

entertainment.title: Kristin Chenoweth to Honor Late Dolly Parton With Gay Men’s Chorus of Los Angeles at Holiday Shows
entertainment.summary: "Celebrating my queen Dolly Parton with the Gay Men's Chorus of Los Angeles? It just doesn’t get any better," said Chenoweth, who will hit the stage at Saban Theatre on Dec. 12-13.
entertainment.body:
The Gay Men’s Chorus of Los Angeles will honor the late Dolly Parton at back-to-back holiday concerts next month and the group has recruited a very special guest to join and pay respects through song.

Emmy and Tony Award winner Kristin Chenoweth will hit the stage with GMCLA for A Very Dolly Holiday!, which will take place Dec. 12 and 13 at Saban Theatre in Beverly Hills, Calif. The chorus, which is kicking off its 48th season, will honor the iconic Parton by performing some of her hits and beloved favorites like “Coat of Many Colors,” “I Will Always Love You,” “Light of a Clear Blue Morning,” “Islands in the Stream,” “Hard Candy Christmas” and “9 to 5” along with holiday favorites like “Happy Xmas,” “Where Are You Christmas?,” “O Holy Night,” “The Christmas Song” and “Let It Snow.” Related Stories Music Dolly Parton Lands Three Posthumous Grammy Nominations Lifestyle Hollywood's Latest Must-Have Luxury? Listening Rooms

“Kristin Chenoweth is one of the great theatrical and vocal talents of our time, a true ally to our community, and someone we’ve been hoping to welcome for quite some time,” said executive director and producer Lou Spisto. “We are absolutely thrilled to have her join us, particularly now, as I can’t imagine a more perfect occasion than A Very Dolly Holiday! Kristin’s deep affection for Dolly Parton, both as an artist and as a person, makes this collaboration especially meaningful. To have a Broadway legend join us in celebrating the ultimate icon and sharing the joy, love and spirit that Dolly represents is something truly special.”

Said Chenoweth: “Celebrating my queen Dolly Parton with the Gay Men’s Chorus of Los Angeles? It just doesn’t get any better. I’ve been a fan of the chorus forever, and I’m so excited to get to take the stage with these fabulous men for the first time. We’re going to give the audiences a show they won’t forget.”

Most recently, Chenoweth, best known for a range of roles from Wicked to Pushing Daisies, most recently produced and starred in Broadway’s The Queen of Versailles . entertainment.title: Hollywood’s Top 25 Legal Troubleshooters
entertainment.summary: Criminal charges, custody fights, contested fortunes — meet the lawyers who handle the problems agents can’t negotiate away
entertainment.body:
Logo text In Hollywood, having a lawyer on speed dial can mean only one of two things. A deal is imminent, or a jury is deliberating. If it’s the latter, chances are the attorney on the other end of the line is on this list.

The 25 Legal Troubleshooters on these pages handle the problems agents can’t negotiate away: criminal charges, custody fights, contested fortunes and who gets to sell the Lakers. Their firms represent stars, moguls and heirs, although lately the L.A. Public Defender’s Office has been giving them unexpected competition. The lawyers themselves are attracting attention, too. Brian Steel has a Drake song named after him; Laura Wasser has a fashion campaign. Others spend their days explaining why a chatbot shouldn’t rewrite your trust.

This firmspent the year representing famous clients facing charges of murder, rape and sex trafficking. Agnifilo and Geragos followed their defense of Sean “Diddy” Combs with Harvey Weinstein’s third trial, which ended in a hung jury, while another client, Oren Alexander, Kim Kardashian’s former real estate broker, was convicted of sex trafficking alongside brothers Tal and Alon. (Tal was represented by Deanna Paul, now a partner at Geragos & Geragos.) Friedman Agnifilo, meanwhile, helped take the death penalty off the table for Luigi Mangione, then pressed to dismiss his state murder case on double jeopardy grounds following his federal plea. But the firm’s most incendiary client this year has nothing to do with Hollywood: Winston Lee is one of seven former Cornell fraternity members accused in a civil suit of drugging and gang-raping a fellow student.

The Parks and Recreation alum recently shared why he has kept his and wife Katherine Schwarzenegger ’s kids Lyla , 6, Eloise , 4, and Ford , 2, in the dark when it comes to his career in the spotlight.

“I haven’t quite told my kids what I do for a living so it’s a little weird to show them my movies,” Pratt explained in an exclusive E! News interview at the premiere for his new Apple TV film The Way of the Warrior Kid Nov. 19. “They’ve started watching some movies and this is definitely appropriate for kids of my kids’ ages. The 47-year-old—also dad to son Jack , 14, with ex Anna Faris —said that while his oldest is aware of his fame, he hasn’t felt ready to introduce his younger kids to his profession.

Of course, he wasn’t ruling out the concept of showing the film, which hits Apple TV Nov. 25, to at least his daughters down the line.

“I’ll have to check with Katherine,” he said, noting that Jack, “has already seen it and he loves it.”

But Pratt emphasizes that his eldest son has certainly proved he can handle any pressure that comes his way.

“Just recently my son Jack was studying for an A Gov test and it was really complicated stuff and they’re getting into some hard academics,” Pratt recalled, “and he was looking at an answer and I said, ‘I don’t know if that’s the right answer or not. entertainment.title: Why Teen Misty From Yellowjackets Looks So Familiar
entertainment.summary: The teen version of Misty Quigley in "Yellowjackets" is played by a former child star who featured in a beloved Disney Channel series.
entertainment.body:
Kailey Schwerman/Paramount+ Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The fan-favorite "Yellowjackets" character Misty Quigley is played by Arizona native Samantha "Sammi" Hanratty in the show's teen timeline, and she may seem familiar to a lot of viewers. If you can't help but wonder where you've seen the actress before when you're watching teen Misty's scenes, it could well be because you're a "Shameless" fan: Hanratty had a recurring role in Season 8 of the hit Showtime dramedy as Kassidi , the bad-influence love interest of Carl Gallagher (Ethan Cutkosky).

Like most of Carl's girlfriends in "Shameless," Kassidi quickly reveals herself to be manic and obsessive. She was too much for many of the Gallaghers, and even the actress herself found her a lot to deal with. "Every episode I would read something and be like, 'I can't believe we're doing that,'" Hanratty told Cosmopolitan about her time as Kassidi, who falsified documents so she and Carl could get married. It may seem like Hanratty has been typecast as an unstable oddball, but her "Shameless" character was actually a departure from the roles she had played prior to that.

A lot of Hanratty's early projects were family-friendly and/or aimed at Christian viewers. In 2014 she featured in the faith-based comedy film "Mom's Night Out," and in 2015 she played an adopted daughter in the Lifetime made-for-TV film "Seeds of Yesterday." It was only with her recurring role in the WGN America horror series "Salem," which she joined in 2014, that Hanratty really started delving into darker roles. She played the character Dollie Trask, who went into hiding after her friends got kidnapped.

In an interview with PopSugar in 2022, Hanratty elaborated on her decision to play more deranged characters like Misty and Kassidi. "I love this industry and telling stories about imperfect people," she said. "Like with 'Yellowjackets,' each person is imperfect and messy, but that's the reality of who we are behind closed doors. And so, getting to tell a story like that, it feels like part of what God put me on the Earth to do."

entertainment.title: Harvey Mason, Rufus Reid & More Are Named 2027 NEA Jazz Masters: Full List

entertainment.body:
Harvey Mason has watched his son Harvey Mason Jr. become CEO of the Recording Academy and one of the most visible people in the music field. But jazz fans know Mason Sr. as a celebrated drummer, composer and producer in this own right. And now he’s a Jazz Master, so declared by The National Endowment for the Arts.

The Jazz Masters Fellowship is the nation’s highest honor in jazz. The Arts Endowment, in collaboration with the DC Jazz Festival, will honor this year’s five recipients in a tribute concert on Monday, April 5, at Arena Stage in Washington, D.C., and streamed online.

“Through their remarkable artistry, leadership and dedication to nurturing future generations, the 2027 National Endowment for the Arts Jazz Masters have worked to advance the distinctly American art form of jazz,” Mary Anne Carter, chairman of the Arts Endowment, said in a statement. “We look forward to partnering with the DC Jazz Festival to celebrate their contributions and the enduring power of jazz.”

“The DC Jazz Festival is deeply honored to partner with the National Endowment for the Arts in celebrating these five extraordinary Jazz Masters,” said Sunny Sumter, president and CEO of the DC Jazz Festival. “Through artistry, innovation and lifelong dedication, these remarkable individuals have influenced generations, preserving jazz’s rich legacy while inspiring its future.”

Since 1982, the National Endowment for the Arts has awarded 186 fellowships to leading figures in jazz. The fellowships, awarded only to living individuals, are $25,000 and can be received just once in a lifetime.

entertainment.title: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Hunts Down $21M in Box Office Previews
entertainment.summary: Joseph Zada leads the cast for the sixth film in the Lionsgate franchise that last hit theaters with 2023 prequel 'The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.'
entertainment.body:
Logo text The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping is ready for battle in its opening weekend at the box office .

The sixth film in the Lionsgate franchise grossed $21 million in Thursday previews before hitting 4,018 North American theaters on Friday. This gives it the second-best previews figure for the franchise, behind only the $25.2 million that 2013’s The Hunger Games: Catching Fire collected and besting the $19.7 million that the original Jennifer Lawrence -led film The Hunger Games earned when launching the franchise in 2012. The first Hunger Games went on to gross $152.5 million domestically in its debut frame, while Catching Fire holds the top-grossing launch in the series by opening with $158.1 million. Related Stories Movies 'I Play Rocky' Stars Unite With Original 'Rocky' Producer for Film's 50th Anniversary Celebration Movies The Sound of Rocky: How an Anthem Was Born

Lionsgate had projected The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping to gross north of $80 million , but other sources expected that it would open much higher and potentially earn between $100 million and $130 million, which now appears the more likely outcome. Adapting author Suzanne Collins’ prequel novel that was published last year, director Francis Lawrence ‘s movie carries a production budget of roughly $150 million as it revitalizes the franchise in telling a story set 24 years before the events of the original 2008 book.

In the new film, Joseph Zada stars Haymitch Abernathy, providing the backstory for the character whom Woody Harrelson brought to life in the first four movies. The cast for Sunrise on the Reaping also includes Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin and Maya Hawke.

The Hunger Games franchise’s five films have surpassed $3.3 billion at the global box office, with the series coming off of its lowest-performing entry with 2023 prequel The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes . Starring Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer, that one disappointed in opening to $44 million domestically before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million.

Sunrise on the Reaping holds a 67 critical score on Rotten Tomatoes as it lags behind the franchise’s first four movies but bests the 64 percent approval for Songbirds & Snakes . In his THR review , chief film critic David Rooney wrote that the new film “delivers on emotion and brutal spectacle.”

entertainment.title: The Short-Lived James Bond Jr. TV Show Didn't Actually Star The Famous Spy's Son
entertainment.summary: Back in the early 1990s, the James Bond franchise came to television in the form of a confusingly-named cartoon series.
entertainment.body:
MGM Television Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover You would be forgiven for assuming that the titular character of the 1991 cartoon "James Bond Jr." is the son of MI6's legendary super spy James Bond, aka 007, but he's actually his nephew. The reason the youngster is called James Bond Jr. is because his own father — 007's brother — is also named James Bond. The show inexplicably suggests that every male Bond is given the first name James. If that's not confusing enough, Jr. never even mentions his father, but always talks about his uncle James, viewing him as a role model and an inspiration. He even introduces himself with the iconic, "Bond...James Bond Jr."

Taking cues from his uncle's missions, Jr. gets launched into his own derring-do adventures, enlisting the help of some of his fellow classmates at the Warfield Academy boarding school. His allies include Horace "I.Q." Boothroyd, the grandson of the classic Bond quartermaster "Q," and Gordon "Gordo" Leiter, son of CIA Agent Felix Leiter. With the aid of his own high-tech gadgets and the family charm, Jr. thwarts the plans of the terrorist organization S.C.U.M, which stands for Saboteurs and Criminals United in Mayhem. While 007 never actually makes an appearance in an episode, some members of S.C.U.M include old Bond villains, like Dr. No and Oddjob.

MGM Television Movie producer Kevin McClory's legal battles with James Bond creator Ian Fleming are well documented. It all started when Fleming decided to write a Bond novel (1961's "Thunderball") based on an unused screenplay he'd penned with McClory. When he found out he wasn't going to be credited, McClory sued. As well as a cash payout, he was granted certain rights.

McClory went on to produce the movie version of "Thunderball" (as well as the Sean Connery-led "Never Say Never Again," which was based on the same Bond tale), and in 1988 he announced plans to create an animated children's TV show called "James Bond vs. S.P.E.C.T.R.E" (it was in "Thunderball" that S.P.E.C.T.R.E first appeared). There were a lot of great cartoons in the '80s , and McClory saw an opportunity to bring Bond into that sphere.

At the time, the movie rights to Bond were held by Eon Productions. Execs decided to get ahead of McClory by creating their own cartoon: "James Bond Jr." was born. It ran for 65 episodes and spawned a Marvel comic book as well as a video game adaptation, but it's barely remembered today outside of its appropriately great opening theme. That's where the relationship ends when it comes to any real Bond connection.

entertainment.title: ‘Glee’ Cocreator: ‘Sadness’ Over Cory Monteith & Naya Rivera’s Deaths Will ‘Be a Part of’ Show Reboot
entertainment.summary: "We’re still figuring a lot of it out," Ian Brennan said in an interview of the reboot rumored to include Lea Michele.
entertainment.body:
Gleeks may have been delighted when Glee ‘s official social media channels announced on Oct. 21 that the musical dramedy would be returning for a reboot. Despite the good news for fans, show cocreator Ian Brennan warned that it’s not going to be all good times when the show returns.

“You’re catching these characters at a totally different part of their life,” Brennan told Variety in an interview published Thursday (Nov. 19). “The timing of these characters thinking, ‘Maybe that was the best time in my life, being in that choir in high school’ and then once you think that you’re like, ‘Oh, that show’s going to work.’”

What’s more, two core characters are obviously missing, something that would unsurprisingly play a part in the characters’ lives in the reboot. Star Cory Monteith, who portrayed Finn, died at age 31 in July 2013, while the show was between seasons. Glee would go on to pay tribute to the actor in the third episode of season five, which included the character’s death, though not a cause of death. (Monteith died after mixing alcohol and drugs, according to the B.C. Coroner’s report at the time.)

Naya Rivera , who played Santana, died in an accidental drowning in July 2020 at age 33, five years after Glee wrapped with its sixth and final season in 2015. The actress died while trying to prevent her son, Josey, from drowning while the two were boating on Lake Piru in California. The little boy, who was 4 at the time, was found safe.

“We’re still figuring a lot of it out,” Brennan told Variety of the reboot and two of the stars’ deaths. “That’s going to be part of it, that sadness and that loss. But still in all, I think [ Glee ] is too big of a thing to sort of let lay. There’s something about that feels right right now.”

While the TV producer believes it’s a good time to bring the show back, he admitted to the publication that he didn’t always feel that way about a potential reboot. “I wasn’t that excited about it,” he said, noting that whenever the topic came up, he’d wonder why it should even happen. “For whatever reason, in the last six months or so, I completely did a 180 about it. It just seems the idea is right. I think the time is right. Now I’m really excited about it. It’s going to be a lot of fun.”

Show creator Ryan Murphy had been teasing a potential reboot this year, even telling Entertainment Tonight in September that he had just finished the script. He shared at the time: “Brad [Falchuk], Ian [Brennan] and I, who wrote all the first two seasons, have written something.”

entertainment.title: Yellowjackets Season 4 Premiere Confirms A Long-Running Fan Theory With Major Implications
entertainment.summary: The opening episode of "Yellowjackets" Season 4 confirmed that one of the girls who was assumed dead in the adult timeline actually made it out alive.
entertainment.body:
Kailey Schwerman/Paramount+ Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "Yellowjackets" Season 4, Episode 1 — "Hivemind"

The "Yellowjackets" Season 4 premiere reveals the fate of an important member of the teen cast: Akilah. Although she doesn't get any lines, the episode shows her among the group of survivors who've been rescued from the wilderness. It turns out that, somehow, despite none of the adult survivors having mentioned her in the first three seasons, Akilah survived her time in the wilderness. "Yellowjackets" fans have been hoping this would be the case for years , and now they've gotten their wish.

For a lot of fans, this reveal was a long time coming. Many "Yellowjackets" viewers developed a fondness for Akilah over the years due to her gentle nature and her reluctance to join in on the worst of the mean girl drama. These fans also noted that, although Akilah's absence from the adult timeline did not bode well for her, she had still never explicitly been confirmed dead. As such, there was always a slim chance, some fans argued, that Akilah would make it out alive.

The "Akilah's still alive" theories have taken many forms, one of the most popular being that she has "gone off the grid" in some shape or form. Before the Season 4 premiere, fans often theorized that she stayed behind in the wilderness. That specific theory's now disproven, but an alternative one — that she went back to the wilderness after being rescued — is still technically up in the air.

Colin Bentley/Paramount+ If there's one downside to the big Season 4 premiere reveal, it's that it takes away some of the suspense from the teen storyline. From day one, "Yellowjackets" promised a dark descent into violence and depravity for the girls; there was this idea that nobody (outside the small handful of girls who made it into the show's adult timeline) was safe. The Season 1 finale expanded the list of adult survivors to include Lottie . Season 2 added adult Van, and Season 3 took things further with the reveal of adult Melissa, played by Hilary Swank.

Now, with Akilah's reveal, there aren't any notable teen survivors left whose fates are still up in the air. It's basically just Gen and Robin, neither of whom are particularly beloved by the audience. In other words, the only ones left in the teen, pre-rescue timeline are either confirmed to survive into adulthood or are essentially glorified redshirts. This could sap a lot of the tension out of what was, at one point, the most suspenseful element of the show.

Madonna isn't waiting for Diplo 's call night and day, but she'll answer anyway.

After all, the "Lean On" artist revealed that his longtime friend has a rare gene that lets her get by on less sleep. And while that makes her more accessible to chat, her schedule has had some unforeseen side effects.

"I don't need a lot of sleep," Diplo began on the Nov. 18 episode of the Office Of podcast . "People say that all the time. I think I'm lying to myself. I know one person that has this gene, though, is Madonna because she really only sleeps like three hours a night, every night."

Though Diplo (born Thomas Wesley Pentz Jr. ) isn't hung up on Madonna's mood, he has prayed that he could also work on much less sleep. But he is leaning on some tried-and-true methods to still have a productive day.

"I am really good at taking care of my body. I've learned things that work when you're traveling, like the way I try to exercise when I'm always landing," he explained, "sleeping as much as I can when I can."

entertainment.title: Peak Halftime Show: The A-List Machine Eventizing Pro Games
entertainment.summary: No longer content with just a Super Bowl splash, pro leagues led by the NFL are increasingly booking major music stars for programming. But it’s a balancing act.
entertainment.body:
Nearly 73,000 fans inside Rio De Janeiro’s Maracanã Stadium rocked out to Ricky Martin and Brazilian DJ Pedro Sampaio on Sept. 27, when the duo performed their song “pikito pikito” live for the first time. But they weren’t headlining a concert — they were playing a halftime show.

The NFL has long held global ambitions, but this is the year it leaned into music to serve as a sort of cultural diplomacy. The Rio game, between the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys, may be the best example, combining a global superstar in Martin with a local talent. “There was a lot of preparation and many hours of rehearsals leading up to the performance,” Martin tells The Hollywood Reporter , “but it was one of those experiences where everything came together beautifully.”

He adds, “These are memories I’ll carry with me for a long time.”

In fact, the NFL has seven halftime shows planned this season, kicking off with the Jonas Brothers in Melbourne on Sept. 10, running through The Warning in Mexico City on Nov. 22. It’s also part of a concerted effort to elevate games into cultural events. Just look at Nov. 25, when U2 will perform during a halftime show for Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium between the L.A. Rams and Green Bay Packers. “There’s really this gathering momentum about how we can further eventize some of the parts on our schedule and our calendar,” Hans Schroeder, executive vp and chief media officer of the NFL, told reporters in October.

The league is leaning into halftime shows as the sports world overall has been more heavily embracing music programming in games. FIFA for instance, had its first World Cup Final halftime show this summer, with Coldplay’s Chris Martin curating a lineup that included BTS, Madonna and Justin Bieber. The NCAA, meanwhile, tapped EDM act The Chainsmokers to play a “bridge show” between the two Final Four games. The NHL has dug in, too, tapping Benson Boone to headline the first intermission during this year’s Winter Classic on New Year’s Eve.

“The NFL and all these leagues understand that to grow the game internationally and even domestically for the younger generation, they need to find organic ways to get those eyeballs,” says Tyler Stimmel, a booking agent in UTA’s music brand partnerships division. He handled booking on many of the NFL’s international events this year, including Jonas Brothers, Burna Boy in Paris, The Warning and Drew Baldridge in Munich.

entertainment.title: ‘Josephine’ Will Floor You
entertainment.summary: Filmmaker Beth de Araújo’s story of an eight-year-old who witnesses an assault is nothing short of phenomenal
entertainment.body:
This is the question that an eight-year-old named Josephine (Mason Reeves) asks her dad, Damien ( Channing Tatum ). She’s a sporty kid, the kind of youngster who accompanies her jockish pops on long runs through Golden Gate Park every Sunday morning. It’s during one of these weekly father-daughter bonding sessions that Josephine sprints ahead of her dad and strays off their usual path. Stopping to catch her breath, she sees a female jogger go into a public restroom at the bottom of a hill. Then Josephine watches as a stranger pulls the woman out, knocks her to the ground, and sexually assaults her.

The cops arrest the perpetrator, the survivor goes to the hospital, and eventually, Damien is left with his daughter and that question, hanging in the air. Josephine can’t comprehend what she’s witnessed. Her father doesn’t know how to answer. Instead of comforting or explaining, Damien just resumes their usual training exercises; he’s got to strengthen her up for soccer, he tells his daughter. His intentions are noble. He wants to protect her by pretending nothing’s happened. But Josephine’s father is simply the first adult who fails to help her process the traumatic experience this young girl has gone through. He won’t be the last.

The Grand Jury Prize winner at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, Josephine doesn’t just follow its namesake as she’s forced to navigate a sudden loss of innocence; it sticks so closely to her perspective that you’re allowed to see every confusing gesture, every mixed-message reply, every argument among her parents, and every acting-out response through her eyes. That itself isn’t unusual — most coming-of-age movies let you walk miles in their hero’s Converse All Stars. Yet writer-director Beth de Araújo’s sophomore film handles this shattering take on a kid wrapping her head around trauma with such grace, such delicacy, such force and a lack of false notes, that the work feels seismic even in its silences. It’s not interested in debating how crimes are handled by the cops or the courts, or how society talks around instead of about sexual violence in a constructive way. The movie wants you to reckon with the impact of someone figuring out a foreign landscape filled with unforeseen terrors. Josephine, c’est moi. entertainment.title: Selena Gomez Recalls How Martin Short Accidentally Cut Her Wedding Cake Early: ‘He Looked Like a Little Dog’
entertainment.summary: The Only Murders in the Building stars reflected on the priceless moment during their Jimmy Kimmel Live! interview.
entertainment.body:
Selena Gomez , Martin Short and Steve Martin are the trio that keeps on giving!

During an interview on Jimmy Kimmel Live! Thursday night (Nov. 19), Gomez and Short recalled the hilarious moment when he accidentally cut into her wedding cake before she and hubby Benny Blanco could get a chance.

“It’s insane because I’m blameless in this story,” Short cracked before describing a layout of 15-person sections, one of which housed a small, particularly appetizing cake. “I just assumed it was a cake for each individual [section]; turns out it was the wedding cake.”

After corralling Steve Martin, his fellow Only Murders in the Building star, to try some of the cake, Short cut into it twice before everyone in the section yelled his name in horror. So at the Gomez-Blanco nuptials, the iconic first slice of wedding cake didn’t go to the happy couple — it went to her Emmy-winning costars instead. “The second I cut it, and I realized it was the wedding cake, I turned to Paul Rudd and said, ‘Should we just go?'” Short quipped.

“I love the teeth marks of the fork [from] where he tried to save it,” Gomez joked after Kimmel flashed a picture of the wounded wedding cake on the screen, before Short chimed in, “That might’ve been the booze talking!”

For her part, Gomez remembers her costar being adamant that no one tell her about his blunder, but she was still clueless as to what was going on. Until someone whispered in her ear, “Marty cut your cake.” She kept herself composed and found Short. “He looked like a little dog with his tail between his legs,” she teased, “I heard you ate my cake.”

To gauge the scale of Short’s snafu, he wagered there were “more than 10 [and] less than 1,000” guests at the reception. Nonetheless, Gomez clarified that she intended to have a small “Just married!” cake for her and her new husband instead of giving every guest a slice.

“We will always have that memory together, and honestly I’ll never forget it,” Gomez said. “And I’m grateful that you tried to eat my cake.”

sports.title: Christian Benford and Dorian Williams ruled out, Dalton Kincaid doubtful for Bills
sports.summary: The Bills will be missing a couple of defensive players for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
sports.body:
Head coach Joe Brady announced on Friday that cornerback Christian Benford and linebacker Dorian Williams have been ruled out for Week 11. Benford has been out of practice with a groin injury and Williams is laid up with a calf injury.

Benford has 33 tackles and eight passes defensed in eight starts this season. Williams has 61 tackles, two interceptions, a sack and a fumble recovery while appearing in all nine games.

Tight end Dalton Kincaid has not been officially ruled out at this point, but he’s also on track to miss the game. He is dealing with thumb and ankle injuries.

sports.title: Justin Reid posts farewell message to Saints, New Orleans
sports.summary: The Saints have not announced any move involving safety Justin Reid, but it seems one is coming soon.
sports.body:
Reid asked for his release this week and he posted a farewell message to the team and the city of New Orleans on Friday.

“In life and sports, things don’t always go the way you planned or hoped they would,” Reid wrote. “Unfortunately, this is one of those moments. But that doesn’t change the love and respect I have for this organization or city. I truly want to see this team and this city thrive. No one deserves it more than New Orleans and the Saints.”

Reid joined the Saints as a free agent in 2025 and he started all 24 games he played for the team. He had 118 tackles, an interception and a half-sack in those appearances.

sports.title: Colts release QB Daniel Jones
sports.summary: Colts avoid $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 by removing Jones from the roster.
sports.body:
It accelerates a process that would have begun with the Colts benching Jones to avoid having a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 becoming a full guarantee if Jones were to suffer a serious injury over the balance of the season. Jones would have then asked to be released, and the Colts would have likely done it.

So the Colts went straight to the final move on the chess board.

Jones will, once officially released, go to waivers. If/when (when) he clears waivers, he’ll become a free agent.

That’s the same thing that happened in 2024, after the Giants benched Jones and he asked to be released. He later signed with the Vikings, remaining there for the rest of the season before signing with the Colts in March 2025.

sports.title: Carson Beck dealing with back spasms, Josh Johnson in line to start vs. Chiefs
sports.summary: The Cardinals may have a fourth starting quarterback in four weeks when they play the Chiefs on Sunday.
sports.body:
Rookie Carson Beck is once again dealing with back spasms, which puts veteran backup Josh Johnson in line to start in Week 11.

Beck made his regular-season debut last week in the 34-6 loss to the Rams. He was able to practice in full on Wednesday but was listed as limited for Thursday’s session.

The rookie QB was previously sidelined with back spasms earlier in the season.

“It’s basically just responding to the treatment, see how he feels when he wakes up tomorrow,” head coach Mike LaFleur said in his Friday press conference.

LaFleur added that he doesn’t think Beck will be out multiple weeks with the injury, but he’s unsure at this point.

“You go with the people who know what they’re doing to treat it. It’s not like this is the first time he’s dealt with it,” LaFleur said. “We’ll see more tomorrow.”

If Johnson does start, it will be his first time playing for Arizona in the regular season and add to his long list of clubs. Johnson has appeared in regular-season games for seven teams, including the Jets back in 2021 when LaFleur was the team’s offensive coordinator.

“Cool part is, if it is Josh, I’ve called plays for him before and had a really great experience calling plays for him,” LaFleur said. “So, we’ll go shoot our shot and I expect nothing less from our guys.”

sports.title: Dan Campbell: Tay Martin's special teams tape was so good, I was shocked we got him
sports.summary: Lions wide receiver Tay Martin has been in the NFL since 2022, and he has only four career catches.
sports.body:
That’s because Martin isn’t only a wide receiver, but also a special teams player. And according to Campbell, he’s one of the best special teams players in football, so good a player that Campbell was surprised to learn Martin was available for the Lions to sign in June.

“Tay’s just a heck of a football player,” Campbell said. “I still can’t believe that we got him. I’m just shocked, I couldn’t believe, seriously I couldn’t believe it. His tape last year, his special teams tape. We’re fortunate to have him. He’s a football player.”

The 28-year-old Martin spent three years in college at Washington State, then two more at Oklahoma State, before signing with the 49ers as an undrafted free agent. He has also spent time with the Titans and Commanders, and he was the leading receiver for the UFL’s Columbus Aviators in the spring.

Campbell said Martin is perfectly capable of playing wide receiver in the NFL, and while the Lions haven’t used him there much, knowing that he can catch passes when he needs to while also tackling as well as a defensive player in special teams coverage is a huge boost to the Lions.

“He’s grown as a receiver,” Campbell said. “But the special teams production is outstanding. What he’s able to bring to us from the receiver position — it’s one thing when you get a DB, a safety, a corner, this guy serves that role on special teams, so it kind of buys you a spot, in a good way. He’s a stud. Thank goodness we got him.”

sports.title: Jets improved their special teams coverage by having fullback Andrew Beck handle kickoffs
sports.summary: Only one kickoff has been returned for a touchdown in the NFL this season, and it was allowed by the Jets when kicker Austin McNamara not only failed to make the tackle, but got in the way of his teammates as they tried to run down Raiders return man Dylan Laube.
sports.body:
The solution was taking kickoff duties away from both McNamara, who is the Jets’ punter, and Jason Sanders, who is the Jets’ field goal kicker. Instead, it’s now fullback Andrew Beck, who has been a good special teams player for years in the NFL, who is handling kickoffs. Beck made a tackle last week on what could have been a much longer kickoff return without him, and he said he loves being able to both kick and make the tackle afterward.

“It was the whole reason that I’m out there, and I think it proves that it’s beneficial to have me doing it ,” Beck told Newsday . “Instead of just to get some cool pictures, I’m actually out there doing it for a reason.”

Jets coach Aaron Glenn said when players have a skill set like Beck, with the ability to both kick and tackle, teams need to take advantage of that.

“He’s a unique player that has done a little bit of everything throughout his career,” Glenn said. “We want to utilize that as much as we can.”

Beck kicked in high school but not in college, and he didn’t think he’d be kicking again in the NFL. Now that he has the job, however, he hopes it increases his value to the team, and bolsters his career.

“I think I’ve shown that I can be successful in a couple different positions,” he said. “Hopefully the coaches feel comfortable putting me there.”

It’s almost unheard of for a player whose primary job isn’t punter or kicker to handle kickoffs, although with the dynamic kickoff rule promoting returns, it makes sense for a player who can make tackles to be out there if he’s capable of kicking the ball into the landing zone reliably. Saints safety Justin Reid has also kicked off, although he’s only done it once this season. If the Jets have success with Beck, it might be something that other teams try — and it might make players who have the unique skill set of being both good kickers and good tacklers more valuable.

sports.title: NFLPA names 49ers DL Osa Odighizuwa their Community MVP for Week 11
sports.summary: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that they have named 49ers defensive lineman Osa Odighizuwa as their Community MVP for Week 11.
sports.body:

“I appreciate everything the NFLPA does for us as players, and I’m honored to be named the Week 11 NFLPA Community MVP,” Odighizuwa said. “Giving back to Portland, Dallas and the Bay Area means a lot to me because each of those communities has played a part in my journey. I hope this recognition encourages my fellow union members to use their platforms to lift others up in the communities they call home.”

The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to Odighizuwa’s foundation and he will join the other weekly MVPs in being eligible for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.

sports.title: The Protect College Sports Act proponents are getting desperate
sports.summary: As the Protect College Sports Act languishes in the lame-duck session of the U.S.
sports.body:
The best evidence of this comes from the fact that New York Yankees president Randy Levine, who serves as the vice-chair of President Trump’s Saving College Sports Roundtable, has called out Stephen A. Smith and me for our public opposition to the PCSA.

We’re being challenged by Levine because we’ve been vocal about calling the PCSA what it is — a bill that addresses the so-called “chaos” in college sports by reducing the rights that the players have won in recent years by successfully attacking a system that was littered with antitrust violations. The powers-that-be want Congress to wave a magic wand that will allow antitrust violations to occur without consequence. (I won’t speak for Stephen A. as to why he opposes the PCSA; I respect the fact that he’s willing to take a stand that clearly conflicts with the position of his employer.)

Levine made his case against Stephen A. (and Michael J.) in an interview with Charles Gasparino of the New York Post .

“One thing that has really annoyed me is the bogus argument put out by agents and their pundits such as Stephen A. Smith of ESPN and Mike Florio of NBC,” Levine said, adding that we “continually misrepresent that student athletes have had and will have no voice, and that is untrue.”

The problem isn’t they’ll have “no voice” later. It’s that they have “no voice” now. The process is being run not by the players but by the NCAA and the schools. The players aren’t claiming that there’s “chaos"; they benefit from the collapse of decades of antitrust violations flowing from the simple fact that the various schools huddled under the umbrella of the NCAA, which issued strict rules limiting what players can receive in exchange for playing college football.

Also, the characterization of me as one of “their pundits” means that Levine believes my opinions aren’t the product of my own authentic beliefs but that I’m somehow in the pockets of the agents representing college football players. While that is just plain false, the accusation isn’t surprising. We’ve caught wind of at least one media member who was offered a significant payment for a social-media post supporting the Protect College Sports Act. (I don’t know who specifically made the offer, but I know it was made.)

Levine called me in September , on the same day that Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) showed up on ESPN’s College GameDay to promote the PCSA. Levine began by basically calling me stupid for not realizing that collective bargaining is an impossibility for college sports.

sports.title: Brock Purdy: Practicing at altitude was the right move, for sure
sports.summary: When the 49ers play the Vikings this weekend, they'll do so at the altitude of Mexico City at Estadio Banorte.
sports.body:
That’s why the team is in Colorado Springs this week to practice at the Air Force Academy to get acclimated. The altitude at Colorado Springs is comparable to that of Mexico City, at over 7,000 feet above sea level.

Quarterback Brock Purdy told reporters on Thursday that he appreciates being at altitude this week to prepare.

“It’s a real thing. I think it’s been nice to be here, practice and get some workouts in,” Purdy said, via transcript from the team. “Even just obviously doing meetings and just living here for a week. It’s been a real thing that we’ve had to adjust to, and I’m glad that we’re here. I think it’s the right move, for sure. Obviously, Mexico City is going to be in a higher elevation than this, but overall, it’s going to be tough for everybody. We’re not living in it year-round or anything like that, so I don’t know. It’s going to be a part of the game for sure.”

Purdy was on the team the last time the 49ers played in Mexico City back in 2022, so he has some understanding of what awaits him. But that was before Jimmy Garoppolo’s injury put Purdy in line to start.

“Obviously, I didn’t play, but just warming up and being there in the game, seeing guys come off the field and seeing them pretty exhausted. It’s a real thing and I think we’re all ready for it,” Purdy said. “For me, I remember those kinds of things, so I’ve just got to be on top of it and prepare for it.”

Kickoff between the Vikings and 49ers is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday night.

sports.title: Geno Smith set for full practice on Friday

sports.title: Puka Nacua serving suspension while on IR raises an important question
sports.summary: The news that Rams receiver Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension while on injured reserve raised plenty of eyebrows, because on the surface it seems very convenient.
sports.body:
It seems convenient because it is convenient. More accurately, it’s strategic.

The suspension is the result of a negotiation between the league and Nacua. In lieu of taking the process to a full-blown hearing before Judge Sue L. Robinson, whose findings of fact ( e.g. , “no violation was committed”) cannot be appealed by the NFL to the Commissioner, the two sides reached a compromise. They made a deal.

It happens every day in civil and criminal courts throughout the country. Controversies get resolved by negotiation. The mutual uncertainty — one side will win, one side will lose — becomes an outcome that, ideally, both sides don’t like but they’ll accept.

So the league, which may have been concerned that Nacua wouldn’t be suspended at all, agreed to a three-game suspension. Given the timing of the deal, the league necessarily agreed to let Nacua serve the suspension while otherwise unable to play.

The NFL didn’t have to do that. It could have dragged its feet. It could have rolled the dice on the decision to be made by Judge Sue L. Robinson. The league ultimately negotiated, and accepted, a situation that allows Nacua to engineer the process in a way that suspends him at a time when he otherwise wouldn’t be playing.

The league realizes that many will disagree with the outcome. That’s why the initial statement regarding the suspension was followed by an email that said this:

“A player’s injury designation does not delay discipline or prevent a suspension from being served.

“Consistent with prior cases, the suspension begins when it is imposed.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other. In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan Marino era, when two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks battled for AFC supremacy. Kelly and the Bills made four consecutive Super Bowl appearances while Marino never returned after his lone trip following the 1984 season. These days, the rivalry belongs mostly to Buffalo. Since Josh Allen arrived in Western New York in 2018, he’s gone 14–3 against Miami, including a playoff victory. The Dolphins have managed to sneak in three wins — just enough to make Allen and the rest of Bills Mafia angry before the next meeting. But the Dolphins coming to Buffalo this week look very different from the team that challenged the Bills’ hold on the AFC East just a couple of seasons ago. Tua Tagovailoa, Tyreek Hill, and Jaylen Waddle are gone. So are Minkah Fitzpatrick and Bradley Chubb, who now wears a Bills uniform. De’Von Achane is still in Miami but sidelined with an injury. And with starting quarterback Malik Willis also on injured reserve, Kyle McCord is preparing for just his second NFL start. Miami may have a new look, but that doesn’t mean everyone on its sideline is unfamiliar with Buffalo. Several members of Jeff Hafley’s coaching staff have faced the Bills in previous stops around the league, while others have crossed paths with the coaches now leading Buffalo. sports.title: Aidan Hutchinson: That's the last time I go airborne
sports.summary: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said he isn't going to tell players to stop celebrating big plays because of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL, but Hutchinson is going to be making some changes on his own.
sports.body:
In a post to his Instagram account, Hutchinson made his first public comments since suffering his injury last Sunday. Hutchinson leaped in the air after sacking Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his knee went out upon landing.

Hutchinson wrote that he has “jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me” and that it will “never make sense” why things played out the way that they did. He added that he does know he will come back stronger from the injury and “that’s the last time I go airborne.”

Hutchinson closed the post with a message asking his Lions teammates to “hold down the fort til I’m back.” That won’t be until 2027, but Hutchinson has shown once already that he can make a full recovery from this kind of injury so there is some light at the end of the tunnel in Detroit.

sports.body: We’ve all gotten the same advice at some point in our lives, likely pre-kindergarten. “If you can’t say something nice, don’t say anything at all.” I’ve also pointed out how embedded it is in my personality to never take an opponent lightly. That’s why for years I’ve been accused of writing articles about doom and gloom takes on how bad teams are to be feared. So here’s my latest one of those. Combining all the above, I decided to play off another cliche, that everyone has a hidden talent. Which I keep referencing but no one seems to ask about it so either you’re not reading my articles at all, or I’ve already explained things so well that my rule of four is super well known in football circles. I’m optimistic it’s the second thing, but here’s a test. sports.title: As he did with the Giants, Colts QB Daniel Jones is struggling, right after getting paid
sports.summary: Jones was awful again in Thursday night's loss to the Texans.
sports.body:
Jones was awful in Thursday night’s loss to the Texans, continuing the worst season of his career — which comes after the Colts signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract in the offseason.

It’s not the first time Jones has performed poorly after getting a big deal. In fact, that’s all Jones has done throughout his NFL career.

Jones’ career started when the Giants made the surprising decision to select him with the sixth overall pick in the 2019 NFL draft. That earned him a four-year, $25.7 million contract, with the Giants having a fifth-year option. Jones didn’t live up to expectations on that rookie contract, and was playing some of the worst football of his career when his third season ended early with a neck injury, so the Giants declined his fifth-year option.

But Jones then played very well in his fourth year, leading the Giants to a surprise playoff berth and a win in the wild card round. That led the Giants to sign him to a four-year, $160 million contract in 2023, committing more money to him than his fifth-year option would have cost. Jones responded to that with a fifth season in which he played poorly, suffered another neck injury and then suffered a season-ending torn ACL.

Jones returned in 2024 but was so bad the Giants first benched him, then cut him. Jones spent the rest of that season on the Vikings’ practice squad.

In 2025 the Colts signed him to a one-year contract, and he responded by winning a quarterback competition with Anthony Richardson and then playing the best football of his career early in 2025 as the Colts jumped out to an 8-2 start. He started to struggle down the stretch in that season, and then his season was cut short by a torn Achilles tendon, but the Colts were so impressed by his start that they signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract in March.

And now, in the first year of that contract, Jones is worse than ever. His 13 interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the NFL this season and already a career-high, with six more games to play. He’s paired that with just seven touchdown passes. He still hasn’t had a single game this season with more touchdowns than interceptions. His 65.4 passer rating is a career low. His 30.3 QBR is a career low. His 58.4 percent completion rate is a career low. His 5.6 yards per pass average is a career low. Jones was once an effective runner, but his 2.9 yards per carry average is also a career low. Any way you slice it, Jones is worse than ever.

sports.title: Bills to retire Andre Reed's No. 83 in 2027

sports.body:
Andre Reed piled up more catches, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns than any Bills player while helping the franchise to four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s and the Bills announced that they will be enshrining his No. 83 alongside the numbers of his longtime teammates Jim Kelly, Thurman Thomas and Bruce Smith at some point during the 2027 season. All four players are also in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

“He’s one of the main reasons I’m up on that wall ,” Kelly said, via the team’s website. “He’s one of the main reasons I’m in the Pro Football Hall of Fame; it takes both of us. When your quarterback goes in, usually you’re probably going to have a receiver or two go in. . . . To have Andre for my whole career was just totally awesome. I thought it should have been done a few years ago, but I’m glad that it’s getting done, and I’m glad I’m able to be here and celebrate his going on the wall to join me, Bruce and Thurman.”

Reed had 941 catches for 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns over 15 seasons in Buffalo. He was added to the franchise’s Wall of Fame in 2006 and voted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.

sports.title: Ashton Jeanty's bad season running the ball overshadows his receiving production
sports.summary: Jeanty is second in the NFL in both catches and receiving yards for a running back this season.
sports.body:
First running back drafted to last running back in the yards-per-carry rankings? Bust. Case closed.

Except it’s not that simple. There’s no excusing the Raiders’ awful rushing offense and Jeanty’s role in it, but it’s also unfair to talk about Jeanty without acknowledging that he’s one of the best receivers out of the backfield in the NFL.

Jeanty has 46 catches this season, second only to Cincinnati’s Chase Brown among NFL running backs. And Jeanty has 417 receiving yards, second only to San Francisco’s Christian McCaffrey. There are a lot of running backs who get praised for what they can contribute in the passing game -- Detroit’s Jahmyr Gibbs, Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson, Pittsburgh’s Jaylen Warren -- and Jeanty has produced more in the passing game than all of them.

Jeanty’s 17 receiving first downs are tied with McCaffrey for the most of any running back in the NFL this season. Although Jeanty has only one rushing touchdown this season, he has three receiving touchdowns, tied for the second-most among NFL running backs. (Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker has four.)

On Sunday against the Seahawks, when Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza struggled in his first NFL start, Jeanty was his leading receiver, with four catches for 46 yards. With the Raiders trying to mount a comeback in the fourth quarter, it was Jeanty turning a short pass into a 38-yard gain that got the Raiders into range for the field goal that made it a one-possession game. The Raiders lost, and Jeanty deserves his share of the blame for their inability to do anything on the ground, but the loss would have been worse if not for Jeanty being available as an outlet receiver for Mendoza.

Jeanty hasn’t been the player the Raiders thought they were getting after he was college football’s leading rusher at Boise State. But his contributions to the Raiders’ offense are real, even if they’re not spectacular.

Afterwards, Montgomery gave the credit to the offensive line, which has been subjected to quite a bit of criticism this season.

“Everybody on our offense, on the O-line , we should believe now because we can do it as long as we stick together and we stick to fundamentals,” Montgomery said, via the Houston Chronicle . “With them guys up front, they catch a lot of heat. They did a hell of a job.”

At 4-6 the Texans still have an uphill battle to make the playoffs. But they traded for Montgomery in the hopes that he could have big games late in the season while they’re fighting for a playoff berth, and on Thursday night, Montgomery and the Texans’ offensive line did that.

sports.title: Shane Steichen on Daniel Jones remaining the starter: "We'll evaluate everything"
sports.summary: Anthony Richardson could finally get a chance to show what he can do.
sports.body:
Asked by reporters after the 26-3 loss to the Texans whether Jones will remain the starter, coach Shane Steichen said, “We’ll evaluate everything.”

The No. 2 quarterback is 2023 top-five pick Anthony Richardson. On Thursday night, he got a garbage-time drive in the fourth quarter. The three-and-out, which started at the Indianapolis 39, consisted of Richardson running for two yards and throwing two incomplete passes.

It was Richardson’s second appearance of the season; in Week 8, he got a couple of mop-up drives when the Colts trailed the Jaguars, 42-7.

At some point, Richardson deserves a real chance to play. How much worse can the Colts’ offense be?

The Colts were outgained by the Texans, 354 yards to 167. They converted one of 11 third-down tries. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes, for 144 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception.

There’s a business reason that points to the Colts eventually getting Jones off the field. His contract has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027. It vests in March. They’ll inevitably bench Jones to keep him from getting an injury that would keep the Colts from releasing him before the injury guarantee converts to a full guarantee.

That’s what the Giants did to Jones two years ago. He then requested, and received, his release.

The same thing could be happening, sooner rather than later, for Jones in Indianapolis. Which means that he could be available to another team.

sports.body: Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are decidedly anything other than apex hunters. That the NFL can still sell this product to anyone is an incredible feat. Yet football fans continue lining up to see awful teams take on each other. It’s not that this one is without some interest, which is due to a few star players among both Houston and Indianapolis. The issue is that as Buffalo Bills fans, you’re settling in to watch the 3-6 Texans take on the 3-7 Colts. Those two teams are a combined 6-13 — which, if you’ve done the math, is less total wins than the 8-1 Bills have on the season. Neither of these teams was supposed to flop this season, though the writing was on the wall for Indianapolis. But Houston? It’s been an epic collapse for the Texans in 2026. A once-mighty defense has proven feckless far too often this season, which has some saying that head coach DeMeco Ryans could be warming the very seat he sits on in Houston. Fair or not, the NFL is a production-based industry. If you’re like me, the game will be on simply because it helps fill the room a bit this evening. You may also share my passion for the Thursday Night Football crew, and their pre-/postgame coverage. If nothing else, there’s also the chances to see the Texans in their Nike Rivals uniforms — and yes, they sure did again steal the Oilers’ vibe. Are you looking for a reason to root on one team over the other here? What you favor depends on who to cheer on to victory. A Houston win helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule/strength of victory, which matters most for NFL teams with postseason hopes on life support. Instead, you may prefer seeing the Colts win simply so it “harms” the slotting of 2027 first-round pick they sent to the New York Jets. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 11 of Thursday Night Football. Maybe this one also turns into a decent game, like a few suspect snooze-fests in primetime before it. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills announced that they will retire wide receiver Andre Reed’s No. 83 jersey at some point during the 2027 NFL season. While the team did not announce when it will happen, they did announce that it will happen, giving fans the news that the retirement ceremony will happen sometime during next season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBills/status/2123567003025784832?a=eiDWs2sPcy4ZrR46DXg&s=20] Reed is Buffalo’s franchise leader in targets (1,585), receptions (941), receiving yards (13,095), and receiving touchdowns (86). He played in Buffalo for 15 seasons, earning seven consecutive Pro Bowl nods from 1988-1994. He was named Second-Team All-Pro by the Associated Press in 1989 and 1990. A fourth-round draft choice out of Kutztown State University in Kutztown, PA, Reed was a key piece of a Buffalo team that made 10 playoff appearances, five AFC Championship Game appearances, and four Super Bowl appearances during his time with the franchise. At the time of his retirement, Reed ranked No. 3 all-time in receptions, and while he has since slipped to No. 23 all-time, it doesn’t dampen his accomplishments at all. sports.title: Christian Parker considered not staying with the Cowboys
sports.summary: The Cowboys have removed play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
sports.body:
Parker told reporters on Thursday that he decided to process the “significant” disappointment by remaining in his job, albeit with the most important role taken away.

“That would have been running from it,” Parker said as to the possibility of resigning.

As to whether it will be awkward moving forward, Parker said, “I think it’s only awkward if you make it, and we don’t have to make it that way.”

But it will be awkward. The defensive coordinator isn’t fully coordinating the defense. And it’s not like the situation in Denver, where the head coach assumed the play-calling duties from the coordinator. Parker’s biggest responsibilities were given to someone other than the head coach — a consultant who arrived just last month.

The cleanest approach for the Cowboys, given the team’s obvious lack of confidence in Parker, would have been to fire him. But that would have come with a buyout of the balance of his contract. And owner/G.M. Jerry Jones doesn’t like paying coaches to not work.

Jones likely hopes Parker will eventually realize that the situation isn’t sustainable and (as the lingo goes) “self-select.” That avoids the buyout and conclusively ends the inherently awkward situation.

sports.body: Despite a convincing win over the New York Jets, national analysts remain divided on whether Buffalo deserves the NFL’s top spot. The Buffalo Bills walked out of MetLife Stadium with a 31-12 victory over the New York Jets, but apparently a 19-point divisional win isn’t enough to impress everyone. Heading into Week 11, Buffalo remains firmly entrenched among the NFL’s elite, with four of our eight tracked national outlets ranking the Bills No. 1 and the remaining four placing them at No. 2. Interestingly, two outlets moved Buffalo in opposite directions following Sunday’s victory. ESPN dropped the Bills from first to second, while Sports Illustrated bumped them from third to second. The result? Buffalo’s average ranking remained exactly where it was last week: 1.50. While national analysts might disagree about which team deserves the top spot, there’s little disagreement that the Bills belong in the conversation. It’s not as though the Bills struggled to put points on the board. Buffalo scored 31 points, generated 389 yards of offense, and kept the Jets out of the end zone entirely. Was it a flawless performance? Absolutely not. The Bills converted just two of their 10 third-down opportunities, and the defense allowed New York to sustain several extended possessions. However, Buffalo also produced three second-half touchdown drives totaling just seven plays and 2:49 of possession. James Cook rushed for 157 yards, including a 74-yard touchdown, while DJ Moore contributed 90 receiving yards and a score. Buffalo found ways to win comfortably without needing everything to go perfectly. Power rankings aren’t simply about the previous week’s final score. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills are 8-1. I really don’t need to say anything more than that, do I? But since I know someone is going to try to argue, let’s get a few things out of the way. Don’t come at me with the number of backup quarterbacks the Bills have faced. How about we talk about the fact that those quarterback changes have forced Buffalo’s defense to adjust its game plan in the middle of a game? And don’t come at me with strength of victory, either. A lot of those teams looked pretty strong on paper when the schedule came out. Joe Brady has had his team ready to play week after week. Some wins have been fun. Some have been downright ugly. But every single one of them counts exactly the same in the standings. The Buffalo Bills are 8-1. They have the AFC East all but locked up at the midway point of the season, and they’re sitting in the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Is there still plenty of work to do? Absolutely. Do they control their own destiny? Yes. We know all of that. But we also know that somewhere along the way, the Bills might have a bad day. And there are other teams whose wins — or losses — can give Buffalo a little breathing room if that happens. So, let’s see who we’re rooting for — and against — this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC standings at the start of Week 11 - Buffalo Bills (8-1) - Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) - Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) - Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) - Denver Broncos (7-2) - Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) - Cleveland Browns (6-4) - New England Patriots (5-5) - Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) - Baltimore Ravens (4-6) - Houston Texans (3-6) - Indianapolis Colts (3-7) - New York Jets (2-8) - Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) - Miami Dolphins (1-8) - Tennessee Titans (1-8) ____________________________________________________________________________ AFC East Miami Dolphins at Buffalo Bills Rooting for: Buffalo Bills Go Bills! Buffalo gets its first shot at Miami this season, and a win would do more than keep the Bills sitting atop the AFC standings. It would also give them their second division win in as many weeks and put a little more distance between them and the Patriots.
